$note: Rules changes the sim tested for the rework (design D34), in order (sim/economy.mjs applies them one by one and re-runs). Every 'after' must equal rules/fieldworks.json; a null 'before' means the key did not exist. The first sim's eight changes (the fortress map) are in this file's history and the design's GDD v1; of them only xp.player_step 200 still applies and it is carried as it stood.

changes.why: Uncapped, the clock fills as fast as the backlog is deep: with 78 orders at the walls on the last day it would fill in under four days, and only the gap would space the hordes. At 30 a day the clock fills at one speed for any backlog of 30 orders or more; the arrivals are days 28, 44 and 60.
At 30 a day, 300 is ten days of gathering and the hordes came sixteen days apart. 150 is five days: arrivals on days 19, 32, 43 and 54.

At seven days the last two hordes came eleven days apart. Ten puts a clear week between an arrival and the next warning: days 19, 34 and 48, with a fourth announced for day 62. That is the fortnight the design asks for.
Half a machine per order made the third horde 40 machines. At 0.4 the sizes are 15, 16 and 33 and still read the backlog as it stood at each warning.
With no growth the castle only ever outgrows the horde. Three more machines each time: 15, 19 and 39, and 46 for the one announced.

Through step 5 every horde was held with nothing asked (target 4 not met): the towers downed each machine on the approach and no wall was touched, so a wall section was worth nothing. At about three and a half times the health and at least twice the damage the horde reaches the wall: the three warnings ask for 8, 2 and 5 finished tasks, and with what the evidence landed inside each warning the castle held all three, the wall at 81%, 89% and 93%.
